messages:
jordan: Hey team — getting a bunch of 429s in prod for ~10m. Dashboard shows burst credits = 0 but we only saw ~10% traffic uptick, not a spike. Any idea?
lia: Sorry about that — can you share your org id and a sample request_id from the response headers? Also which endpoint/model?
jordan: org: org_ABC123, endpoint: POST /v1/completions, model: rw-instruct-large, sample req id: rq_9f3a. Curl + headers attached:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/completions 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_***" 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Burst-Credits-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 8
Content-Type: application/json
```
devon: Thanks — from those headers it looks like your burst bucket was exhausted. Quick explainer: burst credits are a token-bucket that refills at a steady rate. High concurrency or many short requests can drain credits faster than they refill (even if overall TPS only slightly higher).
jordan: Weird — we didn't see concurrency go up. It's mostly a webhooks fan-out: many short requests (20–60ms each) run in parallel but low per-request tokens.
devon: That pattern explains it — lots of short, frequent requests are actually the worst for credit smoothing because each call can consume fixed overhead and trigger credit checks. Two immediate options: batch those requests, or enable per-route smoothing to amortize token usage.
devon: Example smoothing policy we can apply in Console or via the API: 
```
{
  "route": "/v1/completions",
  "smoothing": "burst_aware",
  "bucket_size": "500",
  "refill_tokens_per_min": "60"
}
```
lia: Short-term mitigation: lower client concurrency to ~8, add exponential backoff on 429 (respect Retry-After). We can also apply a temporary manual credit top-up while we diagnose. @emma can confirm.
emma: Confirmed — I added +2000 burst tokens to org_ABC123 for 2 hours, no billing impact. That should buy time while we tune smoothing. :white_check_mark:
mike: FYI infra shipped a tweak earlier to reduce credit charges from ultra-short requests (<50ms) at 2134567990. It's still ramping but should help ~20–30% for patterns like yours.
jordan: Nice — thanks. If this recurs what are the long-term options?
devon: Long term: 1) move to Dedicated capacity (reserved throughput, no burst exhaustion headaches), 2) increase smoothing bucket_size or refill rate for the route, 3) add a small batching/gateway to coalesce webhook calls, 4) implement client-side token-bucket smoothing (small queue + jitter). Happy to run a config test for you.
jordan: I'll try client smoothing + reduced concurrency and report back in ~15m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
